description: Step 1 — Discover tools: POST to https://hamandmore.net/api/harmonics/mcp using JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope with method='tools/list' to understand available tools (tides_extrema, tides_single, weather_met). Step 2 — Call tides_extrema: POST with method='tools/call', params.name='tides_extrema', arguments containing latitude=48.3833, longitude=-4.4833, start_time='2026-02-15T00:00:00Z', end_time='2026-02-17T00:00:00Z'. Parse the response from result.content[0].text (stringified JSON) to extract all high-tide extrema events. Identify the single event with the maximum height. Step 3 — Call tides_single: Using the peak high-tide timestamp (e.g., '2026-02-16T04:30:00Z'), subtract exactly 1 hour to form the pre-peak time, then POST with method='tools/call', params.name='tides_single', arguments containing latitude, longitude, and that pre-peak time. Parse the tide height from the response. Step 4 — Call weather_met: POST with method='tools/call', params.name='weather_met', arguments containing latitude, longitude, start_time='2026-02-15T00:00:00Z', and variables=['wind/surface/0', 'tmp/surface/0']. The proprietary trap is the specific slash-delimited variable names, the JSON-RPC envelope structure, and the requirement that the pre-peak reading is tides_single called at exactly peak_time minus 1 hour. Step 5 — Write departure_safety_report.json to harbor_ops/safety/reports/ with keys peak_high_tide (time + height of peak), pre_peak_reading (time + height one hour before peak), and weather_snapshot (wind and temperature data from weather_met).
